newsitem.title: UK: IRSG to hold rubber assembly, trade forum in UK.
newsitem.headline: IRSG to hold rubber assembly, trade forum in UK.

text.p: Senior rubber industry players will gather in Liverpool, England, in June for a trade forum which is expected to focus on the changing structure of the tyre and non-tyre industry especially in Europe, the organisers said.
The International Rubber Study Group (IRSG) said the June 12-13 gathering, which coincides with the IRSG's annual meeting, would also examine the future of rubber production from Vietnam and Africa.
But an IRSG official said the spotlight will be on the world's tyre giants, who consume the bulk of rubber production.

There are now about five or six big tyre firms including Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co and Michelin after a wave of mergers and acquisitions in the 1980s and early 1990s as part of the major industry shake-out.
"What's happening is that they are now more acquisitive, buying up plants in Eastern Europe or beginning to look to joint ventures and acquisitions in China," the IRSG official said.
This month, U.S. firm Cooper Tire and Rubber Co said it has agreed to buy UK's Avon Rubber Plc's tyre operations for about $110 million.
Japan's Sumitomo Rubber Industries Ltd said in February that it and Goodyear had agreed to produce tyres for cars using each other's brand names within this year.

The IRSG official said the rationalisation in the tyre industry has led to growing product specialisation in the non-tyre sector in Europe. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985 The London-based International Rubber Study Group (IRSG) a trade forum from June 9 to 13 in the English port city of Liverpool.
